claims.text: The integrated ML/ab initio framework can identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity more accurately than conventional prediction methods.
The framework combines machine-learning models trained on vibrational spectra and chemical-disorder metrics with ab initio phonon simulations.
The target high-entropy alloys are near-equiatomic multicomponent mixtures.
The target alloys exhibit significant chemical disorder.
Temperatures from room temperature to approximately 500 K are relevant to the proposed thermal-insulation applications.
Chemical disorder critically influences phonon scattering in the compositions to which the framework is intended to apply.
Chemical disorder and complex atomic-scale heterogeneity enhance phonon scattering.
Machine-learning models can detect subtle variations in vibrational properties and disorder metrics.
Variations in vibrational properties and disorder metrics indicate the intensity of phonon scattering.
Using these variations improves prediction of low phonon thermal conductivity relative to semi-empirical or standard ab initio methods.
The integrated framework will provide an approximately 20% improvement in accurately identifying low-phonon-thermal-conductivity alloys.
The framework may be less effective when microstructural heterogeneity dominates thermal transport.
The framework may be less effective when electronic contributions dominate thermal transport.
The framework's applicability is expected to be limited to 300–500 K.
TDTR or a comparable technique can be used to benchmark the predicted phonon thermal conductivity.
Failure to achieve at least a 20% improvement over conventional methods across a statistically significant sample set would falsify the hypothesis.
